chronicle: At the Marchward trestle, Rhinofire drew the shape of what lies north from two reluctant sources: a duelist's field account of a hand going black and a listening face, and an exile's admission that the upstream structure is a pre-Transition authentication site holding the Council's backup purification sequence — gone silent eight months ago, and perhaps listening still. One final question — what should I not let it hear? — found the edge of what Eredan will carry. He refused it, finally, and returned to his barley.

turns.player: Ask the hostel-keeper if anyone else has come through from the northeast trail recently — one more voice before you commit the direction.
turns.summary: The hostel-keeper describes a lone traveler from the Disputed Zone cutoff, asking after the north road; he left a sealed, unmarked note behind.
turns.narration:
The hostel-keeper is a broad woman with flour on her apron and the unhurried manner of someone who has heard every kind of question and stopped being surprised by any of them. She's wiping down the counter when you put the question to her — anyone through from the northeast trail lately, before the melt turned the ground soft?

She thinks for a moment, setting the cloth down. "Two, maybe three days back. A man alone, coming down from the Disputed Zone cutoff. Kept his hood up, which people do, so I didn't press. But he paid in valley coin and he asked about the road north — not the way to the Redline, the *other* north, the one that goes into the Zone proper." She picks the cloth back up. "He ate, he slept, he was gone before I came down in the morning. Left the bed neat, which I appreciated."

Marrow shifts on the rafter above the counter — you didn't see it get up there, but here it is, watching the keeper with the specific calm attention it reserves for things that are concluding. The keeper glances up at it, unsurprised in the way border-town people learn not to be surprised by anything, and goes back to wiping.

"He left something, actually. Forgot it or didn't want it." She reaches under the counter and sets down a small square of folded paper, sealed with a plain wax thumb-press. No mark, no name. "If you're going that direction anyway."

redline-duelist-marchward.name: Redline duelist
redline-duelist-marchward.role: Mercenary contractor, recently through the Disputed Zone
redline-duelist-marchward.description: Worn leathers, a horizontal scar across the collarbone, the economy of someone who earns with her body and has stopped pretending otherwise.
history: [d1] Spoke unprompted about the survey crew she passed on the northeast trail eight days ago — a man holding his hand like it burned, crew moving fast with no gear.
[d1] Read: relieved, professional. Spoke freely because the Marchward demands plain speech. Information given, weight transferred. Still watching the exile sideways.
[d1] Did not react to the exile closing — recognized it as a man hitting his limit, no performance of surprise. Looking at the treeline.

[d1] Filled in the missing detail — the hand pressed flat to the sternum, not the side; fingers black from the second knuckle and still going; the man's face listening, not pained. Noted the crew moved in deliberate, agreed-upon silence — not panic.
[d1] Finished her cup, stood, and departed without ceremony — obligation to plain speech met, no further business at the trestle.
knownFacts: Eight days ago she passed a Council survey crew retreating fast from the northeast trail in the Disputed Zone — no map-cases, one man's hand pressed against his thigh as if burned
She asked what was happening and was told 'the ground is doing something' — she left south rather than investigate
Her relief is professional — weight transferred, not guilt shed. She is assessing the exile the way a fighter watches a sparring partner.
The burned hand was pressed flat to the chest, fingers black from the second knuckle — an active process, not aftermath
The affected surveyor had a listening expression — as if hearing something the others could not
The crew's silence was deliberate and coordinated, not panicked — they had decided together not to speak of what they saw
redline-duelist-marchward.statusNote: Departed the trestle, back toward the hostel interior.

stillhold-exile-marchward.name: Eredan
stillhold-exile-marchward.role: Former Stillhold resident, now sheltering at the Marchward
stillhold-exile-marchward.description: Older, patched grey robe, hands that have been kept still for a long time and are starting to shake. Eats carefully.
history: [d1] Volunteered, quietly, that the Council lost contact with the upstream structure — it is there but no longer answers. Said it like a weight set down.
[d1] Read: guilt as much as fear. His confession was a weight set down, not a report delivered. He is afraid of what he knows and what knowing it makes him part of — not of Rhinofire.
[d1] Asked directly what the structure was and what 'no longer answers' means — closed the question: 'I've said what I can say.' Not fleeing, not hostile. The limit is older than this conversation.
[d1] The listening-face detail from the duelist landed somewhere — he has not moved or responded, but his stillness reads as recognition, not indifference.
[d1] Did not surface a reaction to the listening-face detail despite the silence offered. Face averted, still, barley bowl untouched.
[d1] Their name is revealed: Eredan (was known as "Stillhold exile")

[d1] Named himself — Eredan, no surname. Confirmed the structure is a pre-Transition authentication site that held the Council's backup purification sequence. Went quiet eight months ago — present but not answering. Final words: 'Be careful what you let it hear.'
[d1] Asked directly to come north to the structure. Refused with a single word and drew the conversation closed. Now eating his barley — the first time he's touched it.

[d1] Asked what Rhinofire should not let the structure hear. Refused with the same words as before — 'I've said what I can say' — but the refusal landed differently: not bureaucratic, something decided. He is protecting himself, not just information.
knownFacts: He spoke like a man confessing, not reporting — the lost structure carries personal guilt for him, not merely institutional knowledge.
Distinguishes between what he knows and what he can say — the rest is sealed, not forgotten
The listening expression on the burned surveyor may mean something to him specifically — his stillness after the duelist described it is pointed
The upstream structure is a pre-Transition authentication site
It held the sequence for the Council's secondary (backup) purification system — not the main flow
It stopped responding eight months ago — not destroyed, not sealed, still present
He will not go to the upstream structure — the refusal is final, not reluctant
His limit is not about what he knows — it is about what he is still willing to be responsible for. The last question reached that line.
skillsObserved: institutional knowledge of the Stillhold and the Council

facts: [d1] Two separate clusters of people at the Marchward used the word 'substrate' unprompted — a mason's apprentice and a Marcher trader who then looked at his hand as if he'd felt something. The flickering has reached even the border-town.

[d1] The burned hand of the retreating surveyor and the exile's phrase 'no longer answers them' sit beside the substrate-talk — whatever is happening in the upper structure may be the same stirring felt in people's hands at the Marchward.

[d1] The surveyor's listening face — hearing something no one else could, hand pressed to his chest as the blackness spread — reads less like a wound and more like a signal received. Something at the upstream structure may be transmitting, not merely malfunctioning.

[d1] Eredan's warning — 'be careful what you let it hear' — implies the authentication site may be listening. An eight-month silence followed by renewed activity suggests it did not stop; it may have been waiting for something.

chronicleCache.hash: d0|b|c|q|L1|To right the wrongs of the world
chronicleCache.text: You have become someone who carries a grievance older than your own name — a fury at wrongs not yet righted, a moral weight that sits in the chest like a coal still finding its heat. The Marchers know your face now, have registered your presence among them the way a wall registers a first crack: noted, not yet tested. The Ashwardens and the Unmakers have heard nothing particular about you, which means the world still holds its breath. Even the Stillhold watches from a wary distance, as if they sense something in you that hasn't declared itself yet. You have done nothing of consequence — not yet. That is the whole of the pressure.
